content.title: European (UEFA) 2026 World Cup qualifying: Playoff results, dates, scores, qualified teams - NBC Sports
content.text: UEFA qualifying for the 2026 men’s World Cup is done, with four teams outlasting 12 others in a dramatic March week of second-round, single-elimination fixtures around Europe.MORE — How will 48-team 2026 World Cup work? First round groups were won by England, France, Croatia, Portugal, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Switzerland, Belgium, Austria, and Scotland, earning automatic berths in the 2026 World Cup.MORE — UEFA World Cup qualifying scenarios for final dayAnd the 12 group runners-up and four UEFA Nations League entrants met in four pathways, with Bosnia and Herzegovina, Sweden, Turkiye, and Czechia sealing places in the 2026 World Cup. Here is everything that went down from the first match to the two playoffs finals that reached penalty kicks en route to the 2026 World CupEuropean (UEFA) World Cup second round resultsPlayoff Path ASemifinalsItaly 2-0 Northern Ireland - Recap, highlightsWales 1-1 Bosnia & Herzegovina (Bosnia & Herzegovina win 4-2 on penalty kicks)FinalBosnia & Herzegovina 1-1 (4-1 pens) Italy — Recap, video highlightsPlayoff Path BSemifinalsUkraine 1-3 SwedenPoland 2-1 AlbaniaFinalSweden 3-2 Poland — Recap, video highlightsPlayoff Path CSemifinalsTurkiye 1-0 RomaniaSlovakia 3-4 KosovoFinalKosovo 0-1 TurkiyePlayoff Path DSemifinalsDenmark 4-0 North MacedoniaCzechia 2-2 Republic of Ireland (Czechia win 4-3 on penalty kicks) - Recap, highlightsFinalCzechia 2-2 (3-1 pens) DenmarkEuropean (UEFA) 2026 World Cup qualification formatFirst round (March 21-November 18, 2025): Twelve groups of 4-5 nations play round-robin, home-and-away. Group winners qualify for 2026 World Cup. Runners-up reach one of four playoff paths.Second round (March 26-31, 2025): Twelve group runners-up plus the four top remaining UEFA Nations League group winners are drawn into four semifinal and final paths. Four path winners qualify for 2026 World Cup.Which UEFA nations qualified for the 2026 World Cup after the first
